scope: Thirteen new bounded source guides and seven previously inspected collections curated without new history/source/adequacy changes.

profiles.name: Abenaki
remainingGaps: Broaden the collection through substantial, fully inspected historical scholarship, oral-history projects and public writing addressing particular places and families throughout the homeland. The current selection centers Odanak and Wôlinak rather than claiming complete regional coverage.

Compare colonial missions, military violence, settlement and land restrictions through original records and community interpretations. A broad historical synthesis cannot settle each event, local chronology or territorial claim.

Develop a carefully attributed account of contested contemporary identity and recognition claims, including the relevant nations’ positions, state records, and the perspectives and evidence of those whose claims are disputed. The May 2022 Odanak report is one primary position, not an independent adjudication.

Inspect more of Laurent’s dictionary and later language scholarship with appropriate orthographic context; seek dated evaluations of community language teaching rather than inferring results from project announcements.

Follow the black-ash work, Wôlinak planning goals, Odanak governance discussions and preliminary archaeology protocol through later community reports, distinguishing plans, adoption and demonstrated outcomes.

Add more first-person public accounts by women, young people, artists, basket makers and land users, and seek community review of scope and interpretations. The twelve-source target is separate from an adequacy assessment, a completed deep dive or community review.

profiles.name: Abihka
remainingGaps: Seek additional Arbeka-authorized public history and review of preferred names, the town relationships summarized here, and the cultural suitability of archival descriptions.
Inspect the original Dorsey Fife affidavit, the relevant land-allotment ledgers and census pages, and the maps behind the 2023 report rather than relying solely on its archival synthesis.

Deepen the distinction between historical Abihka, Abihkutci, Abihka-in-the-west, Talladega and Choccolocco communities; similar spellings and reused names do not by themselves establish identical locations or institutions.

Expand community-specific evidence on language learning, schooling, livelihoods, women’s experiences, and life beyond the selected public reports. No present speaker, membership, or population total is asserted.
Add community-led accounts of Natchez relationships and of removal and allotment experiences; older authors’ assimilation claims and one leader’s biography do not represent every family.
Follow the Oxford educational and preservation partnerships with dated evaluations of outcomes, distinguishing plans from completed work.

profiles.name: Absentee Shawnee
remainingGaps: Develop more community-authored family and local histories, especially experiences of the Big Jim and White Turkey communities beyond institutional summaries.

Reconstruct landholding under the 1872 legislation and 1890–1891 allotment process through tribal interpretation and primary records; do not equate rights to individual allotments with a blanket claim of communal title.
Add an Absentee Shawnee account of twentieth-century displacement around Little Axe and Lake Thunderbird, with carefully evaluated records of land acquisition and community rebuilding.
Follow up the January 2026 language initiatives with dated community reports on classes, participation and learning; no current fluent-speaker total is asserted.
Expand community perspectives on education, livelihoods, arts and stewardship, and check cultural suitability and permissions before reproducing artworks, recordings or ceremonial material.

Confirm the latest consolidated constitutional and code amendments with the Tribe when using these materials for a precise legal question; archived enactments and funding agreements have different dates and purposes.

profiles.name: Acoma Pueblo
remainingGaps: Add a fully inspected critical edition of the 1598–1599 trial, translated Acoma testimony, and specialist historical work. Compare casualty, sentencing, and implementation claims without treating colonial proceedings as neutral evidence or repeating uncertain numerical totals.

Deepen Acoma-specific accounts of the 1680 revolt, Spanish return, seventeenth-century mission labor, and community rebuilding; the included IPCC resource supplies regional context rather than that full local history.

Trace the current status of the Rio San José settlement through later Pueblo statements and enacted instruments, and document water-delivery outcomes. A 2024 request for legislation is not evidence that it became law.

Compare the landholding inventory with current Pueblo records and primary grants, executive orders, statutes, and trust decisions. The inventory is historical and has not been converted into a present boundary map or current acreage claim.
Add direct public interviews and writings by more Acoma artists, scholars, teachers, farmers, women, and young people; expand community life beyond the mesa and beyond the examples represented here.

Seek dated language-program, school, and restoration evaluations while respecting member-controlled access and the Pueblo’s authority over cultural and linguistic materials. No Atlas community review has been recorded.

profiles.name: Achumawi
remainingGaps: Expand band-authored history beyond the Hewisedawi account and named Madesi and Illmawi voices; one band’s experiences cannot represent all nine language-associated bands.
Examine additional primary records of settler violence and forced removal alongside community accounts, identifying whose experiences each record describes.
Document current community-led fisheries and restoration work before describing contemporary management outcomes.
Investigate the final outcome and subsequent history of the 2001 land-transfer proposal; its review and tribal objections do not establish current title.
Read the remaining sections of the language-needs study and later community program reports; early research and announcements do not establish present attendance, fluency, or program capacity.
Track implementation and subsequent policy developments after the 2025 Sáttítla designation, including actual management plans, agreements, and tribal participation.
Continue reviewing the supplied bibliography and seek community editorial review. Fifteen inspected resources are a milestone, not a completed comprehensive history.

profiles.name: Adai
remainingGaps: Compare more community-authored histories and publicly shared family accounts; this profile is an introduction and has not received community review.

Obtain and read the full Pleasant 2013 settlement-location article before adopting its proposed geography. Colonial place names and candidate archaeological sites do not establish a single precise homeland boundary.
Reconcile language classifications through surviving documentation and specialist analysis; neither an old categorical classification nor a modern political affiliation settles linguistic descent.
The Solís translation and Avery study report different baptism totals. Compare the underlying manuscript and alternative translations; baptism entries are not a census of the Adai people.
Verify land-grant and cession chronology against original instruments. The collaborative briefing contains internally inconsistent dates, so this article does not adopt a land-title conclusion.

No present acknowledgment petition disposition, complete documentary petition, current speaker census or comparable membership series was verified. Interview advocacy and dated counts have limited scopes.
The community cultural-center address and state directory disagree on the highway number. Resolve that discrepancy before any later geocoding; do not infer wider territory from a public facility.

Extend coverage of nineteenth- and twentieth-century change, community livelihoods, teaching outcomes and the range of family experiences without generalizing one representative’s account to everyone.

profiles.name: Ahtna
remainingGaps: Add more village-authored histories and contemporary perspectives from Cantwell, Mentasta, Cheesh’na, Kluti-Kaah and other communities; this introduction has not received community review.

Confirm current community-approved language teaching and archive access through authoritative institutions. The lessons, dictionary, interview and archive study retain their own dates; neither current speaker counts nor teaching outcomes are established here.
The publicly linked former Foundation domain identifies itself as an unofficial reconstruction. Its descriptions are not used to verify present programs, contacts, archive holdings or permissions.
Independently listen to and check the Mentasta lesson audio before describing playback or pronunciation beyond the inspected written material.

Follow Gulkana’s January 2024 public review draft through any adoption record and later implementation. Its small mixed-participant survey and internally inconsistent priority counts do not support population-wide percentages or rankings.
Extend the dated Tazlina environmental account with later village evidence; the 2018 article does not establish current ownership, complete remediation or completion of planned work.

Resolve the Community Harvest System report’s inconsistent chart rates and averages against underlying records. Follow recommendations through subsequent regulatory decisions before asserting present conditions or hunting rules.

Compare additional appropriately public family and archival accounts of local displacement and political organizing. Shared earlier research does not make every cited publication an independent confirmation.

Establish suitable rights and community context before reproducing maps or extracting geometry. Historical homeland representations, corporate parcels, park boundaries and private-use locations must remain distinct.

profiles.name: Aundeck Omni Kaning First Nation
remainingGaps: Clarify the internally inconsistent founding-date sentence through community-authorized histories and original records.
Review fuller relocation and family histories, language-program work and community interpretations of the 2024 settlement.

profiles.name: Henvey Inlet First Nation
remainingGaps: Inspect the community history reports and the original works cited by the project.
Add public language, family and cultural accounts without conflating historical clan names and present citizenship.
Read enacted trust documents, later community reports and evaluations before describing outcomes.

profiles.name: M’Chigeeng First Nation
remainingGaps: Read community-authorized histories and the records behind the former West Bay name and nineteenth-century settlement account.
Review selected public language recordings with appropriate language and access context before discussing their content.

profiles.name: Mississauga #8 First Nation
remainingGaps: Establish the compilation’s original author, publication history and fuller community context.
Inspect original records and further community-directed histories before extending personal recollections.
Review public land plans and monitoring reports separately; no legal boundary or current environmental condition is determined.

profiles.name: Serpent River First Nation
remainingGaps: Inspect original industrial agreements, community environmental studies and archival records behind the public timeline.
Add further Nation-published education, language and community-life accounts.
Retain Nimkii Aazhibikoong as a distinct named-community research lead; identity and relationships need their own review before creating an outline.

profiles.name: Sheguiandah First Nation
remainingGaps: Add fuller community-published histories and educational sources beyond this short naming account.
Keep the present First Nation distinct from adjacent municipal history and archaeological interpretations; do not infer ancient-to-present descent from proximity.

profiles.name: Sheshegwaning First Nation
remainingGaps: Add Sheshegwaning-authored historical and language materials, with full community context beyond project reporting.
Verify school opening and governance implementation through dated community records; do not treat design intentions as measured outcomes.

profiles.name: Thessalon First Nation
remainingGaps: Check treaty chronology and original instruments independently; the public history page contains a problematic Niagara Congress date.
Review community-authored history and language sources beyond the two short selected accounts.
Seek newly dated programme descriptions before using schedules, staff lists or outcomes as current information.

profiles.name: Zhiibaahaasing First Nation
remainingGaps: Seek Zhiibaahaasing-authored history and language resources, including community explanations of its names and relationships.
Follow water-project updates without assuming that announced construction or promised benefits have been completed.

profiles.name: Long Lake #58 First Nation
remainingGaps: Add community-authorized historical work beyond the current education-focused starting guide.
Inspect the original history curriculum and underlying archival sources before summarizing earlier periods.
Verify current programmes through newly dated publications; the undated education page includes old plans.

profiles.name: Netmizaaggamig Nishnaabeg
remainingGaps: Review community-authored historical research and the archival records cited by the Nation.
Trace later land-administration stages separately; the2021 announcement and current community account describe different dates and scopes.
Add public language and education resources without conflating Netmizaaggamig with Biigtigong Nishnaabeg.

profiles.name: Pays Plat First Nation
remainingGaps: Inspect original community historical materials and trader/treaty records before extending the early chronology.
Read the2018 agreement and later community publications separately; announcements are not the underlying instruments.
Add public language, education and community-life sources beyond land-administration context.

profiles.name: Mississaugas of Scugog Island First Nation
remainingGaps: Review original records behind the Nation’s relocation and repurchase account.
Add community-directed language, family and cultural publications.
Review later infrastructure reports separately; do not infer present water safety.

sourceCounting: 26 added profile-source contexts; seven curation-only profiles add no content inspections. Repeated publications are not new global works. Identity-only outline evidence is excluded.
provenance: Exact source scopes/dates and individual image credits/rights/complete-available-frame limits retained. No private files or full third-party texts published.
